rationale: Evidence: iteration 8 (kd 2.5, base_speed 1.2, kp 3.5, ki 0, 12 mm sensors at y=0.04 with x in ±0.04) is the best design so far at 395.3. The oval finishes 20 of 20 trials at mean time 1.87 s, which leaves about 1.1 s of headroom under the 3 s limit. The s-bend (progress 0.395) and slalom (progress 0.178) still end off track with about one line-loss event per run. Iteration 9 raised kd to 3.2 and returned a score identical to iteration 8 on every track and metric, so the kd lever appears to have saturated at this operating point. I am not pushing kd further. Speed is now the constraint: at base_speed 1.2 the robot is too slow to finish the s-bend or slalom in 3 s, and the oval margin shows it can afford more speed. Change for this draft: base_speed 1.2 to 1.4, one controller step only. kd stays at 3.2 (a tested value with identical results to 2.5, so no regression risk from the damping side), and kp 3.5, ki 0, line_loss 'last_direction' and the geometry are unchanged, so any change in outcome is attributable to speed. Expected result: oval completion holds with completion_time falling to about 1.6 to 1.7 s; s-bend and slalom progress rise if the extra speed does not push the robot off the tape through the sharper sections. Score of roughly 400 to 500 is plausible. The main risk is that higher speed causes off-track exits on the slalom, which would lower its progress term. If the oval holds and progress rises, the next step is base_speed about 1.6. If the s-bend or slalom fall off track earlier, speed is past the stability limit at this damping and the next draft should return to 1.2 and test a wider sensor row or a different line_loss setting.
